icon noun

a holy image

also holy image

Renaissance

M-O s.v. icon, after Tursellinus (1652): sānctārum imāginum cultōrēs

sāncta imāgō

an icon, a holy image

The classical imāgō, a likeness or portrait (Cic.), with the Church’s sānctus; in church plain imāgō will do. In the Orthodox Church icons are venerated: kissed, censed and given a burning lamp. In the West holy images include statues, and “icon” usually means a painting in the Byzantine manner.

Other words

  • imāgō sacra

    also used · modern · Levi–Bini p. 31, s.v. icona

  • 1īcōn: long o in the nominative (Lewis & Short leaves it unmarked: īcon, ŏnis). Greek εἰκών, with omega in the nominative and omicron in the other cases (εἰκόνος), whence the short o of īconis. Traupman 261 prints īcōn, īconis.

    īcōn1, īconis f. — an image (the Greek word)

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Plin. NH 8.215 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 261, of a computer icon; Traupman 331

    Pliny has it once, of figures. Traupman gives it for the icon on a screen, so it is less clear for a holy one.

Examples

  • Ōsculāre sānctam imāginem.

    Kiss the icon.composed

See also iconostasis, saint, icon.
